sections.content:
Clicking the track didn't change anything either. Hmm. So far: RIGHT, clicking the handle, clicking the track — none of them did anything. Maybe the interaction is with the squares at the bottom. Or maybe the mouse click needs to be on the small blue/sky-colored block at the right end of the track (the "goal" indicator). Or maybe this game is a "drag" game where a single MOUSE click is a mousedown, and a subsequent arrow key moves the held object? Some environments implement drag as a click (select) followed by arrow keys.
Let's test: click the handle, then RIGHT. If the handle moves, then that's the mechanic.
Or maybe the game is: click the small square (the one with the purple cross) to select it, then click the large square to...? Or maybe it's a "copy the pattern" game: the small square is a "palette" and you click the tiles of the large square to paint them?
Wait — let me reconsider. This might be a known game genre: "match the pattern by sliding a slider." The slider handle is at the left end. The small blue block at the right end of the track might be a "stop/goal" marker. The bottom squares: the small one shows the current pattern (purple plus), the large one shows the target (white checkerboard). Moving the slider might rotate/shift the pattern.
But nothing has moved yet. Let's try the click-then-arrow-key combo. Also try clicking the small blue block at the right end (row 20, column 40).
Actually, maybe the mouse coordinates are off: the board is 64x64, and row 20, column 27 is the gray track — I clicked there, but nothing happened. Maybe the click needs to be exactly on the handle's pixel, and then a second click somewhere else drags it? Or maybe the MOUSE action is a "click" that only works on interactive objects, and the handle is draggable via a sequence: MOUSE down on the handle, then MOUSE at the target position? In many of these grid game environments, a MOUSE action at (row, col) is a single click, and drag = two clicks (down, up).
Let's try: click the handle (20,14), then click the track at (20,30) — a drag attempt.
